title: Polydimethylsiloxane-polycarbonate Microfluidic Devices for Cell Migration Studies Under Perpendicular Chemical and Oxygen Gradients
protocol: Design microfluidic channel patterns using commercially available illustration software.
Submit the file for high-resolution transparency photomask printing.
Clean silicon wafers with acetone, isopropyl alcohol, and buffered oxide etch.
Rinse wafers with deionized water and dehydrate with a nitrogen gun.
Spin coat 20 g of SU-8 2050 photoresist onto the wafers at 500 rpm for 15 seconds and then at 2,000 rpm for 30 seconds.
Soft bake the wafers on a 65 °C hotplate for 3 minutes and then at 95 °C for 9 minutes.
Expose the wafers using a mask aligner with designed transparency masks under UV light.
Post-exposure bake (PEB) the wafers at 65 °C for 2 minutes and then at 95 °C for 7 minutes.
Immerse the wafers in SU-8 developer with strong agitation or in an ultrasonic bath for 7 minutes.
Rinse the wafer with acetone and isopropyl alcohol to remove residual SU-8.
Place the wafer and 100 μl of silane into a 6 cm diameter Petri dish in a desiccator connected with a diaphragm vacuum pump.
Turn on the pump for 15 min.
Seal the desiccator with a vacuum for 30 min.
Take the silanized wafers out of the desiccator.
Tape the silanized wafers to 15 cm diameter Petri dishes.
Mix PDMS monomer and curing agent at a 10:1 ratio (v/v).
Degas the mixture in the desiccator setup for 60 min.
Transfer 2 g of the PDMS pre-polymer onto the mold with top-layer fluidic channel patterns to make a thin layer of PDMS.
Place the mold in the desiccator setup to degas the PDMS for 60 min.
Place the mold overnight in a 60 °C oven on a horizontal plane for PDMS curing.
Cool down the mold to room temperature.
Pour an additional 13 g of PDMS pre-polymer onto the mold.
Degas the PDMS in the desiccator setup for 60 min.
Slowly embed a 1 mm thick PC film into the fresh PDMS layer as a gas diffusion barrier.
Expel any bubbles if needed.
Put the mold overnight in the 60 °C oven on a horizontal plane.
Cool down the cured PDMS to room temperature.
Cut the device with a scalpel to an area of approximately 5.5 x 5 cm², which can cover all channel patterns.
Peel off the PDMS slab from the mold.
Punch holes for inlets and outlets using a 2 mm-diameter biopsy punch.
Store the fabricated top PDMS-PC layer away from ambient dust for later assembly.
Pour 11 g of the PDMS pre-polymer onto the mold for the bottom layer.
Place the mold in the desiccator to degas the PDMS for 60 min.
Keep the mold overnight in a 60 °C oven to cure the PDMS on a horizontal plane.
Cool down the cured PDMS to room temperature.
Cut the device to an area of approximately 5.5 x 5 cm², which can cover all channel patterns.
Peel off the PDMS slab from the mold.
Store the fabricated bottom PDMS layer away from ambient dust for later assembly.
Spin coat approximate 4 g of PDMS pre-polymer onto a silanized blank wafer at 100 rpm for 90 sec, then at 3,000 rpm for 4 sec.
Bake the spin-coated wafer in a 60 °C oven overnight.
Place the fabricated PDMS-PC top layer and the wafer with the spin-coated PDMS membrane in an O2 plasma surface treatment machine with the bonding surfaces facing up.
Treat the PDMS surfaces with 90 W of O2 plasma for 40 sec.
Bond the top layer onto the PDMS membrane right after O2 plasma surface treatment.
Place a weight of about 600 g on top of the bonded layers and put them in a 60 °C oven overnight to promote bonding.
Cool down the bonded layers to room temperature.
Cut the membrane bonded to the top layer with a scalpel to an area of approximately 5.5 x 5 cm2.
Peel off the bonded structure from the silicon wafer.
Punch holes at the inlets and outlet of the chemical gradient channel using a 2 mm-diameter biopsy punch.
Place the membrane-bonded top layer and the fabricated PDMS bottom layer in the O2 plasma surface treatment machine, with bonding surfaces facing up.
Activate the PDMS surfaces using the plasma at 90 W for 40 sec.
Attach the top and bottom layers together for bonding immediately after surface treatment.
Place a weight of about 600 g on top of the entire bonded device and put it in a 60 °C oven overnight.
Take the entire fabricated device out of the oven and cool it down to room temperature.
Culture A549 cells in complete growth medium containing DMEM F12 L-glutamine substitute, 10% fetal bovine serum, and 1% antimicrob-antimycotic solution.
Sub-culture by dissociating the cells with 0.25% trypsin-EDTA.
Centrifuge the dissociated cells at 140 x g for 3 min at room temperature to prepare cell suspensions.
Count the cells using a hemocytometer and seed 1 x 10^6 cells in a T75 flask with 10 ml of complete growth medium for microfluidic device experiments.
Place the microfluidic device into an O2 plasma machine and treat it with O2 plasma at 90 W for 40 sec to make surfaces hydrophilic.
Insert two 14 G blunt needles directly into the 2 mm diameter holes punched into the PDMS layer at the chemical gradient channel inlets.
Draw 0.8 ml of ddH2O using a 1 ml syringe with a blunt 14 G needle and inject it into the chemical gradient channel from the outlet until water flows out from both inlet needles.
Prepare 1 ml of 50 µg/ml fibronectin solution by diluting fibronectin stock with Dulbecco's Phosphate-Buffered Saline.
Aspirate the medium from cells cultured since day 0.
Wash the cells with 5 ml DPBS twice.
Add 2 ml of trypsin-EDTA and incubate in an incubator for 5 min to detach cells from flask surface.
Wait until cells are detached and suspended in solution, then add 8 ml serum-free medium (DMEM F12 + 1% antimicrob-antimycotic).
Transfer liquid into a 15 ml conical tube and centrifuge at 140 x g for 5 min under room temperature.
Aspirate supernatant after centrifuging, add an appropriate amount of serum-free medium to make the final cell density 1 x 10^6 cells/ml.
Count cells using a hemocytometer or automatic cell counting instrument.
Inject serum-free medium from the outlet of the chemical gradient channel using a 1 ml syringe with a blunt 14 G needle until medium flows out from both needles at inlets.
Inject 200 μl of the cell suspension from the outlet of the chemical gradient channel.
Observe the cell culture chamber in the device under a microscope.
Place the device into a humid container and keep it in a cell culture incubator for 5 hr.
Prepare SDF-1α at a concentration of 100 ng/ml in serum-free medium.
Draw serum-free medium with SDF-1α into one 3 ml syringe.
Draw serum-free medium without SDF-1α into another 3 ml syringe.
Connect the syringes to high-purity tubing.
Set up the syringes on a syringe pump at a flow rate of 1 µl/min.
Make 15 ml of 1 M NaOH solution.
Make 15 ml of 200 mg/ml pyrogallol solution.
Draw the NaOH solution into one 15 ml syringe.
Draw the pyrogallol solution into another 15 ml syringe.
Connect the NaOH syringe to high-purity PTFE tubing.
Connect the pyrogallol syringe to high-purity tubing.
Set up the syringes on a syringe pump at a flow rate of 5 µl/min.
Take the entire device out after a 5 hr incubation.
Place the device on a 15 cm diameter Petri dish.
Fix the device in the Petri dish using adhesive putty.
Transfer the Petri dish to a live cell imaging microscope in an incubator.
Connect tubing from the syringes for chemical gradient generation to the inlets of the chemical gradient channel.
Connect the outlet to tubing leading to a waste reservoir.
Turn on the syringe pump with the syringes for chemical gradient generation.
Connect high-purity tubing from the syringes containing NaOH and pyrogallol to the inlets of the oxygen gradient channel.
Connect tubing to the outlet to collect the waste.
Turn on the syringe pump with the syringes for oxygen gradient generation.
Add about 15 ml of ddH2O to the Petri dish to keep the device moisturized.
Set up the live cell imaging microscope for time-lapsed image capture.
Take an image every 15 min.
Transfer captured image files to a computer.
Analyze the images using ImageJ with the Manual Tracking plugin.
Use Chemotaxis Tool software for analysis.
Prepare an oxygen-sensitive fluorescent dye solution at a concentration of 5 mg/ml in water.
Draw the oxygen-sensitive dye solution into two separate 3 ml syringes connected to high-purity tubing.
Set up the syringes on a syringe pump with a flow rate of 1 µl/min.
Connect the tubing from the syringes to the inlets of the chemical gradient channel.
Connect the outlet to tubing leading to a waste reservoir.
Turn on the syringe pump for chemical gradient generation.
Measure the fluorescence intensity using an inverted fluorescence microscope.
Pass excitation light through a 470 ± 20 nm optical filter.
Collect emission light through a 515 nm long-pass emission filter using a cool CCD camera.
Connect high-purity tubing from the syringes containing NaOH and pyrogallol to the inlets of the oxygen gradient channel.
Connect tubing to the outlet to collect waste.
Turn on the syringe pump for oxygen gradient generation.
Collect fluorescence images of the oxygen-sensitive dye flowing in the cell culture chamber.
Stop the flow for oxygen gradient generation.
Disconnect all the tubing to the oxygen generation channel.
Connect high-purity tubing from the gas cylinders to the outlet of the oxygen gradient channel.
Collect fluorescence images of the oxygen-sensitive dye flowing in the cell culture chamber when flowing air into the tubing connected to the oxygen gradient channel.
Collect fluorescence images of the oxygen-sensitive dye flowing in the cell culture chamber when flowing pure nitrogen into the tubing connected to the oxygen gradient channel.
Collect fluorescence images of the oxygen-sensitive dye flowing in the cell culture chamber when flowing pure oxygen into the tubing connected to the oxygen gradient channel.
Estimate the oxygen gradients by analyzing the fluorescence images using the Stern-Volmer equation according to References 10 and 11.
